children.translated_text: Homage to the Supreme Lord, the Lord of the <s>Gaṇas</s>, the trident-bearer,
who is seated on the lotus of consciousness, whose form is divided into four.
Having meditated upon the letterless (<s>avarṇa</s>), soundless, all-pervading Supreme Lord (<s>Parameśvara</s>),

children.text: vyutthāne yoginām itthaṃ śivatvaṃ jāyate sphuṭam ||
children.translated_text: thus in emergence [from <s>samādhi</s>], the state of <s>Śiva</s>-ness arises clearly for yogins.
Then the yogin, infused with <s>Śakti</s>, whose body is <s>nāda</s> (cosmic sound) and <s>bindu</s> (point of light),
attains the <s>dvayasampatti</s> (fulfillment of the dual — <s>Śiva</s> and <s>Śakti</s>), established in the state beyond all support (<s>nirādhārapada</s>).
Since these two verses were proclaimed from the mouth of <s>Śiva</s> in the <s>Āgama</s>,
this pure exposition of the yogic treasury (<s>yogikoṣa</s>) proceeds here.

children.text: ahaṃkāramayī bhūmir buddhibhūmeḥ parā hi sā |
children.translated_text: The ground consisting of <s>ahaṃkāra</s> ('I'-consciousness) — that is indeed higher than the ground of <s>buddhi</s> (intellect).

children.text: tayā vyāptam idaṃ sarvaṃ saiva jñātā vimuktidā ||
children.translated_text: By it all this is pervaded; it alone is the knower and the bestower of liberation.
The supreme <s>Śakti</s>, of the nature of <s>saṃvid</s> (consciousness), undifferentiated, belonging to the Supreme Lord —
that very <s>jñānaśakti</s> (power of knowledge) manifests again in the form of <s>mantra</s>.
<s>Ahaṃkāra</s> ('I'-consciousness) is remembered as <s>mantra</s>, having the essential form of <s>Śiva</s> and <s>Śakti</s>.

children.text: yad atrādyam avarṇākyaṃ sa śivaḥ parameśvaraḥ ||
children.translated_text: What is here the first, called <s>avarṇa</s> (the phoneme 'a') — that is <s>Śiva</s>, the Supreme Lord.

children.text: nādabindvātmakaṃ yat tu dvitīyā śaktir aiśvarī |
children.translated_text: And that which is of the nature of <s>nāda</s> and <s>bindu</s> — that is the second, the sovereign <s>Śakti</s>.
This pair has been declared as the seed-essence (<s>bījabhūta</s>) in all that is moving and unmoving.
By this [phoneme 'a'], having the form of a glowing ember, all the phonemes (<s>varṇas</s>) are sealed.
Therefore the yogins, contemplators of reality, call it <s>Śabdabrahman</s> (the Absolute as Word).
Having meditated upon the breathless and soundless, through <s>paśyantī</s> (the visionary level of speech), undifferentiated,
by the union of pure consciousness-reflection (<s>cinmātrāmarśa</s>), one would dissolve into the supreme state (<s>parapada</s>).

children.text: tathā hi siddhair ādiṣṭaṃ kvacit siddhāntasaṃgrahe |
children.translated_text: For thus it has been instructed by the <s>siddhas</s> (perfected ones), somewhere in the <s>Siddhāntasaṃgraha</s>:

children.text: nābher ūrdhvaṃ vitastis tu kaṇṭhādhastāt ṣaḍaṅgulam ||
children.translated_text: above the navel is one <s>vitasti</s> (span of twelve finger-breadths), and below the throat is six finger-breadths.

children.text: hṛdayaṃ madhyadeśe tu padmaṃ tu hṛdi madhyataḥ |
children.translated_text: The heart (<s>hṛdaya</s>) is in the middle region, and the lotus is in the center of the heart.

children.text: tatra madhye sthitā sūkṣmā karṇikā tripathopagā ||
children.translated_text: In the middle of that lotus is situated the subtle pericarp (<s>karṇikā</s>), approached by three paths.

children.text: tatra madhye hy akāraṃ tu svātmatattvaṃ vyavasthitam |
children.translated_text: In its very center, the phoneme 'a' (<s>akāra</s>) is established as the principle of one's own Self (<s>svātmatattva</s>).
Within the 'a' is the supremely subtle, characterized as the principle of pure consciousness (<s>cinmātratattva</s>).

children.text: tasyāpy upāsā kathitā vijñāne bhairavena tu |
children.translated_text: Its worship too has been spoken of by <s>Bhairava</s> in the <s>Vijñānabhairava</s>:

children.text: abindum avisargaṃ ca akāraṃ japato mahān ||
children.translated_text: 'For one who recites the phoneme "a" (<s>akāra</s>) without <s>bindu</s> and without <s>visarga</s>, O great one,
a great flood of knowledge, the Supreme Lord (<s>Parameśvara</s>), suddenly arises, O Goddess!'
At the place of the ear, supportless, is the second, the sovereign <s>Śakti</s>,
the seed-essence <s>Kuṇḍalinī</s>, whose nature is <s>nāda</s> and <s>bindu</s>.

children.text: prāṇaśaktir iyaṃ dehe hakārākhyā nadaty alam ||
children.translated_text: This <s>prāṇaśakti</s> (life-force energy) in the body, called <s>hakāra</s> (the phoneme 'ha'), sounds forth abundantly.
The yogin, having blocked the opening within the ears, should clearly perceive:

children.text: bindurūpā bhruvor madhye viśvasya jananī dhruvā ||
children.translated_text: in the form of <s>bindu</s>, between the eyebrows, the eternal mother of the universe.
She is always perceived by yogins, blazing with her own radiance.
Her reflections are the moon and the sun, in the left and right eyes.

children.text: nirāśrayau tu tau kṛtvā viṣed brahma sanātanam |
children.translated_text: Having made those two supportless, one should enter the eternal <s>Brahman</s>.
This has also been stated in the <s>Vijñānabhairava</s>, a scripture practiced by the <s>siddhas</s>:

children.text: sampradāyam imaṃ samyak śṛṇu devi vadāmy aham |
children.translated_text: 'Hear this tradition (<s>sampradāya</s>) correctly, O Goddess, I shall speak:
<s>Kaivalya</s> (absolute liberation) arises instantly when the eyes are merely fixed [without blinking].'

children.text: saṃkocaṃ karṇayoḥ kṛtvā hy adhodvāre tathaiva ca |
children.translated_text: 'Having contracted the ears and likewise the lower aperture,
ac
kam a
hal
meditating on 'aṃ', one should enter the aperture of <s>Brahman</s> (<s>brahmabila</s>) in an instant.'
[meditating on the phonemic notation:] an
Thus has been sung from the mouths of the <s>siddhas</s>, proclaimed by [<s>Śiva</s>] himself.
By this path, those who are perfected attain the state of the <s>yoginīs</s>.
Born in the land of <s>Jāka</s>, a lion in the forest of <s>Mīmāṃsā</s> —

children.text: harṣadattetināmā yas tasya sūnor iyaṃ kṛtiḥ ||
children.translated_text: he whose name is <s>Harṣadatta</s>: this is the composition of his son [<s>Vāmanadatta</s>].
